newsitem.title: JAPAN: "Independence Day" director to film Godzilla movie.
newsitem.headline: "Independence Day" director to film Godzilla movie.

text.p: Roland Emmerich, director of the hit U.S. movie "Independence Day", was named to film the next Godzilla movie, to be released in 1998, Japanese moviemakers Toho Company announced on Tuesday.

Kyodo news agency and the Yomiuri Shimbun newspaper said Toho and Tri-Star Pictures had signed a deal in which Emmerich would start filming the new monster movie in Hollywood early next year. The two companies did not give details of the contract.
Emmerich has been a Godzilla fan since childhood, Kyodo said.

Toho has made 22 films featuring the fire-breathing monster since the first one, a black and white film simply called "Godzilla" in 1957. The name of the monster is a cross between "god" and a Japanese word that means whale, "kujira".
The latest one, "Godzilla vs. Destroyer", was released in Japan last January and billed as the last Godzilla movie that Toho would make.
But Godzilla fans in Japan and abroad were sceptical, saying Godzilla had always made comebacks after repeatedly perishing in movies.
